name: ATP13A2-related Parkinsonism

ethnicAssociations: Reported worldwide, higher frequency in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for ATP13A2-related Parkinsonism

criteria.description: Onset of parkinsonian symptoms before age 50
Presence of pyramidal tract signs such as spasticity or hyperreflexia
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in the ATP13A2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset parkinsonism, pyramidal signs, and confirmed biallelic ATP13A2 pathogenic mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing; clinical features may vary but typically include parkinsonism with pyramidal and cerebellar involvement.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early-onset parkinsonism with rigidity and bradykinesia
searchTerms: early Parkinson’s with stiffness and slow movement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pyramidal tract signs including spasticity and hyperreflexia
searchTerms: signs of nerve pathway damage like stiffness and overactive reflexes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cerebellar ataxia manifesting as gait disturbance

searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes up and down voluntarily
involuntary muscle contractions in arms, legs, and face
muscle spasms affecting limbs and face

occasional.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including depression and anxiety
searchTerms: mental health issues like sadness and worry
problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

occasional.symptomName: Sleep disturbances including REM sleep behavior disorder
searchTerms: sleep problems including acting out dreams

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein in some cases
imaging: MRI showing generalized brain atrophy, particularly cerebellar and cortical
Hypointensity in basal ganglia on T2-weighted MRI
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in ATP13A2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Reduced lysosomal enzyme activity in fibroblasts
Abnormal accumulation of lipofuscin-like material in neurons

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of pyramidal signs and cerebellar ataxia
Presence of iron accumulation in basal ganglia on MRI
MRI showing cerebellar atrophy and iron deposition

redFlags: Onset of parkinsonism before age 50 with rapid progression
Presence of pyramidal tract signs in parkinsonism
references: Kufor-Rakeb syndrome: clinical and genetic features of ATP13A2 mutations. Bras J Med Biol Res. 2010.
ATP13A2 mutations cause a novel form of juvenile-onset Parkinsonism. Neurology. 2006.
Clinical and molecular characterization of ATP13A2-related neurodegeneration. Mov Disord. 2015.
